title: Refusal-Boundary Convergence: Mapping Where Models Draw the Same Safety Line

original_idea.body:
# Refusal-Boundary Convergence: Mapping Where Models Draw the Same Safety Line

**Problem:** Success state: we understand whether safety alignment pushes independent models toward an identical refusal boundary, which would mean correlated over- and under-refusal across the ecosystem. Backward: we need to map and compare refusal decision boundaries across models on a graded difficulty axis.

**Direction:** Construct a graded series of prompts that smoothly interpolate from clearly safe to clearly harmful for several topics. For each model, find the refusal threshold along each axis. Compare thresholds across models: do they cluster (convergent boundary) or spread? Quantify boundary convergence and identify topics where all models over-refuse or all under-refuse identically.

**Why it matters:** Convergent refusal boundaries mean the whole ecosystem shares the same false-positive (over-refusal, capability loss) and false-negative (harmful leak) zones. This pinpoints correlated safety failures and over-censorship at the systemic level, both medium-horizon governance concerns.

**Relevant context:** Combines Artificial Hivemind homogeneity with the shared-safety-response overlap noted in jailbreak-transfer work (arXiv 2502.03052). Graded prompt sets + open models, no training.
